title: Rescue long-context requests from maintenance-induced admission hang
creator: Mei Chen
description:
Summary: During a routine maintenance window for a subset of Dedicated hosts, we observed an admission hang in the continuous batcher that caused long-context requests to be starved across Hosted and Dedicated tenants and surfaced as customer escalations. Private customers who applied the maintenance bundle without a new upgrade hook also saw degraded tail latency. This ticket tracks the hotfix, cross-environment mitigations, and follow-up robustness work.

Root cause hypothesis: A maintenance-driven drain signal temporarily cleared per-worker admission tokens but failed to release in-progress lease bookkeeping when a scheduled prefetch handshake raced with the drain path. The result was a small set of workers holding taut admission reservations while the dispatcher believed capacity was available, causing the scheduler to prefer new short requests and defer long-context admissions indefinitely (head-of-line inversion + eviction churn against KV cache).

Impact: High customer impact (P0) — several paying customers reported elevated 95/99 latency and token billing anomalies for long-context endpoints during the window. Observed in Hosted regions us-west-2 and eu-west-1 and in Dedicated clusters running maintenance images. Private customers who upgraded without the guard hook reported similar tail degradations; no data leak observed.

Goal: 1) Patch production runtime with a targeted fix that prevents admission leases from leaking during drain; 2) Mitigate impact for Dedicated and Private fleets (manual cordon + staged rolling restart); 3) Add telemetry, cancellation path tests, and an upgrade hook for Private deployments to avoid recurrence; 4) Run a postmortem and surface the safety guard for future maintenance windows.
comments: 2025-02-18 09:22 Mei Chen: Initial SOC alert — 99th latency for /v1/generate (long-context) spiked from 340ms to 1.9s after scheduled maintenance in us-west-2. Triage started. Linked dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/abcd/continuous-batcher?orgId=1

2025-02-18 10:05 Tomás Rivera: Reproduced locally with a maintenance drain test harness. Observed admission lease count mismatch: worker reports reserved slots > dispatcher allowed slots. Suspect race in drain->prefetch handshake. Attaching debug logs and core snapshot in artifacts.

2025-02-18 12:30 Aisha Khan (SRE): Hotfix plan approved. Steps: (A) push runtime patch to Hosted canary pool (B) cordon affected Dedicated pools and run rolling restart (C) provide Private customer guidance for upgrade hook. Communications drafted for CS and affected customers.

2025-02-19 02:14 Tomás Rivera: Deployed hotfix (runtime-1.23.4-hotfix.1) to Hosted canary. Canary shows restored 99th latency to baseline within 15 minutes. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4827

2025-02-19 05:00 Mei Chen: Manual mitigation for Dedicated: we cordoned two impacted clusters and performed staggered restarts — customers reported immediate improvement. Private customers informed with an upgrade hook script; one private cluster applied the hook and confirmed tail recovered.

2025-02-21 11:45 Tomás Rivera: Added per-worker admission-lease expiry (sliding lease) and defensive reclaim in dispatcher if worker fails to ack within timeout. Integration tests added to continuous-batcher suite covering concurrent drain + prefetch scenarios.

2025-02-24 16:20 Natalya Petrov (PM): Communicated incident summary to affected customers and provided timeline + temporary credits for elevated token usage. Working on coordinated postmortem publication by 2025-03-05.

2025-02-28 09:00 Mei Chen: Observability follow-ups: new telemetry flags expose per-tenant stalled-admission counters and KV-eviction churn rate. Alert rule created (Alert ID: STALL-9001) to notify SRE at 5-minute sustained stall. Leaving this ticket In Review pending private upgrade bundle and runbook updates.
